scope: Prospective shared bounded local compiler rule for fullFFN shaping addendum; applies identically to candidate, RR row-safe and packed layouts under synchronized IPR capability.
rule: Given a validated useful page stream and a declared pool of real unselected resident pages, evaluate unchanged useful waves plus all single original-wave prefix splits; optionally all pairs of distinct original-wave prefix splits when max_added_waves=2. All physical waves read4planes using real pool pages where useful pages are absent. Keep exact useful consume order.
prefix_choices: 1..(number of useful pages in original wave)-1; a one-useful-page wave is not split
timing: Use sealed v1 finite-PB strict_no_interval model with one shared fixed capability profile. Never silently rescue with cold_reset or retained CR bias.
selection: Select feasible lowest modeled makespan; tie by fewest added waves, then lexicographic original index/prefix. If none passes, return infeasible. This rule is fixed before fullFFN addendum evaluation, not fit to held-out cost outcomes.
interpretation: This is a deterministic compiler search using kernel geometry and the declared timing contract. Results must be called shared-rule compiler results, not a per-query performance oracle or globally optimal policy.
dummy_pool_contract: Caller supplies true unselected resident pages with plane/block/WL and unselected=True or dummy_unselected_expert metadata. Pool pages must not collide with any requested or already-read physical address. New partial waves use same-block dummy pages; no weight movement or stored copies.
IPR_boundary: Packed pages retain their true existing physical addresses. Adding differing-WL dummy reads invokes the same granted synchronized-IPR capability and must be labeled packed+IPR+shaping, never ordinary same-WL.
cache_boundary: Any signature cache must include physical block/change/active-plane structure and source order; page identifiers alone may be abstracted, block continuity may not.
excluded: changing useful pages or their order
